claim: The public agent API separates backend creation, registration, metadata exchange, request construction, posting, status, notifications, and cleanup.
The operation enum distinguishes READ and WRITE, while memory types and statuses are explicit public contracts.
Basic descriptors carry an address or offset, byte length, and device/file/block identity rather than model-level KV semantics.
Plugin discovery/loading constructs backend engines; it does not establish registered ranges or a successful transfer.
UCX request status drives worker progress when pending requests exist.
The meta package aliases runtime modules from a selected installed backend wheel.
Plugin manager tests distinguish stale API rejection from current API acceptance.
The metadata manager starts last in data construction and stops before data members are destroyed.
effectiveSyncMode upgrades NONE to STRICT if metadata backend threads share the agent caches; RW and STRICT already lock.
createBackend rejects duplicate backend types and illegal combinations before publishing an engine.
Remote-capable engine creation requires notifications and connection information, while local-capable engines connect to self.
Backend capabilities distinguish local, remote, and notification support and expose the transfer lifecycle interface.
Backend creation order populates the memory-type registration candidate vector; this is not a measured global backend optimizer.
nixlBasicDesc has uintptr_t addr, size_t len, uint64_t devId and a deliberately noninitializing default constructor.
Coverage logic checks bounds without treating unsigned overflow as valid and handles the SIZE_MAX unbounded sentinel.
DRAM, VRAM, block, object, and file segment categories describe memory domains, not universally enabled transports.
FiniteFileSegDoesNotCoverOverflowingRange and UnboundedFileSegDoesNotCoverOverflowingRange assert overflow-safe coverage.
UnboundedFileSegCoversFiniteRangeFromNonzeroOffset covers the unbounded file registration case.
Path-mode file registration reserves a unique devId and constructs file metadata before committing the reservation.
The descriptor example exercises construction, copying, overlap checks, and serialization.
registerMem is best effort across candidate backends and returns success if at least one backend registration succeeds.
A local-capable backend loads the local registration view into the self remote section and rolls back an added registration if that load fails.
UCX registration calls memReg and packs a remote key; it does not allocate the caller buffer.
Libfabric validates supported memory types and constructs registration metadata containing caller buffer, length, and device identity.
POSIX path-mode deregistration releases the reserved devId and deletes file metadata.
RegisterDeregisterMemRepeatedTest exercises repeated registration/deregistration through controlled engines.
loadConnInfo accepts unchanged cached connection information and rejects a changed cached value with NOT_ALLOWED.
Connection metadata is inserted into remoteBackends only after the backend load succeeds.
loadRemoteSections merges successful partial updates into the existing shared remote section, preserving weakly bound handles.
Explicit invalidation erases the remote section, disconnects recorded backends, and removes cached connection information.
A failed remote section load invalidates the peer rather than retaining an invalid partial section.
LoadRemoteAfterSectionError verifies failed section load removes peer state and valid reload succeeds for absent and existing peers.
TCPStore metadata invalidation tests explicitly invalidate remote metadata because that backend has no watch.
nixlDlistH owns backend-specific metadata-stride lists and holds a weak remote-section reference for remote lists.
makeXferReq requires local/remote roles, nonempty equal index counts, a common backend, and notification capability when requested.
makeXferReq locks the prepared remote section reference and rejects retired generations before using prepared metadata.
Indexed request construction validates selected indices and paired lengths before passing populated ranges to the backend.
Dense merging requires compatible dense strides and consecutive local and remote index runs; skipDescMerge disables merging.
Ordinary creation uses the first candidate whose local and remote populated metadata succeed, without comparing all backend costs.
PreparedTransfersPreserveBinaryBackendParameters checks length-bearing custom parameters survive prepared request construction.
postXferReq rejects an expired remote registration section before posting backend work.
An active repost checks completion and returns REPOST_ACTIVE if the earlier execution is still pending.
getXferStatus rechecks backend and remote generation only while stored status is pending; completed/error results are cached.
releaseXferReq preserves the public request if backend active release fails and returns REPOST_ACTIVE.
Successful active release nulls the backend handle before deleting the public request to avoid duplicate backend release.
FailedActiveReleaseKeepsRequestPollable asserts pending post, refused release, successful later status, and successful final release.
RejectedRepostTakesNoExecution asserts that a refused active repost does not consume an accepted execution identity.
getNotifs aggregates blobs by sending agent across eligible engines and continues best-effort collection after a backend error.
genNotif selects a notification-capable engine compatible with local or known remote backend state rather than broadcasting across engines.
UCX stores a pending associated notification until data status succeeds and clears it on a data error.
sendNotif moves the message into an active-message send and tracks asynchronous send work on the backend request.
UCX getNotifs progresses workers then swaps queued notifications into the caller list.
NotificationOnly, SelfNotification, and EmptyNotificationPayload cover standalone, local, and empty-payload notification behavior.
NotifyingWritePostedTwice exercises a reused notifying request in the sampled tracing fixture.
UCX advertises DRAM and VRAM memory domains and packs registered-region keys into public metadata.
loadRemoteConnInfo creates per-worker endpoints in a shared connection before inserting it.
sendXferRange maps paired local/remote metadata to endpoint read or write calls and adds endpoint flush work.
SGL posting is conditional on HAVE_UCX_SGL_API, runtime enablement, and WRITE operation.
The backend request retains the shared connection that owns its endpoint.
UCX release cancels incomplete requests and warns; its TODO does not promise rollback of remote writes.
Direct intra-agent and inter-agent test helpers cover host/device paths when supported.
Libfabric conditionally advertises VRAM according to runtime/build paths and validates memory types at registration.
Libfabric prepXfer requires a valid peer connection and prepares fragmented notification metadata when requested.
Without the progress thread, checkXfer progresses active rails before checking completion and completion-queue errors.
POSIX advertises local support only, no notifications, and FILE/DRAM memory types.
POSIX preparation requires self-agent target, local DRAM, target FILE, and equal descriptor counts.
POSIX queue selection rejects simultaneous use_aio, use_uring, and use_posix_aio choices.
Partial read/write assertions verify shrinking remaining lengths and advancing file offsets and buffer pointers.
The libfabric regression checks re-establishment when one peer retains connection state.
The actual wrapper constructs descriptors, backend handles, prepared/request objects, and notification matching state.
Tensor descriptor paths require contiguity and compute byte ranges from data_ptr, element count, and element size.
Post and status bindings translate negative native statuses into exceptions before returning to wrapper string mapping.
Opaque request release sets the released flag only after native release succeeds.
A request finalizer queues a refused native handle in the owning agent leaked-handle list for best-effort later release.
check_remote_xfer_done polls and removes only the first sender message matching its prefix or substring tag.
test_notification_is_consumed_once verifies matching removal, including empty notification payloads.
test_leaked_xfer_handle_is_queued_on_the_agent injects release refusal and asserts deferred ownership of the native handle.
Requests and prepared lists hold weak remote-section references rather than owning caller allocations.
Successful refresh preserves a section, whereas explicit invalidation or failed load retires it and stale handles do not revive after reload.
A completed cached status does not bypass the next post remote-generation gate.
Refused active release returns before public-handle deletion so later polling and cleanup remain possible.
Canceling/releasing UCX requests is resource cleanup with an explicit implementation limitation, not transactional destination rollback.
LoadRemoteAfterSectionError verifies cache rollback for both new and already connected peer state.
Explicit NIXL_TELEMETRY_ENABLE disable overrides configuration captureTelemetry.
Requested capture without an output sink uses collect-only NOP telemetry; a configured directory defaults to BUFFER.
postDuration and xferDuration share the posting timer and should not be added as disjoint durations.
getXferTelemetry requires telemetry enabled and successful completed request status.
Trace identity distinguishes a reusable request from each accepted backend post execution.
Tracing loads requested backend plugins on demand and returns no tracer if none initialize.
Completed-transfer metrics are filtered and inserted as an all-or-none batch into bounded staging.
NonFittingBatchRejectedWithoutPartialInsertion and RejectedBatchDropCountEqualsBatchLength assert batch pressure behavior.
The preparation script measures descriptor construction, registration, prepared lists, and request construction without posting payload transfers.
GetXferTelemetryAPI, GetXferTelemetryCaptureNoSink, GetXferTelemetryAPICfg, and disabled cases assert capture/sink precedence.
The worked DRAM WRITE selects eight bytes at source offset sixteen and destination offset eight.
The example waits until both initiator success and a target notification are observed before cleanup.
Prepared dense/permuted index mappings have different merge eligibility while preserving paired byte semantics.
Failed metadata section loading retires peer cache state and valid reload succeeds.
The active-release recovery test preserves the request through a refusal and later completes/releases it.
Native negative-status exceptions must be handled in addition to Python pending/done string results.
